extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy, theology, and church-state relations (scholars of Hobbes)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of Hobbes's doctrinal standards about ecclesiastical power, sacraments, excommunication, martyrdom, and the limits of ministerial authority as given in Leviathan. Focuses on what counts as ecclesiastical authority, its transmission, effects, and its relationship to civil sovereign power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power Ecclesiasticall is the power to teach/proclaim
rubrics_metrics.description: The Power Ecclesiasticall was in the Apostles; it consisted in a power to proclaim the Kingdom of Christ, and to perswade men to submit themselves thereunto — Ministers are 'our Schoolemasters, and not our Commanders, and their Precepts not Laws, but wholesome Counsells.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes repeatedly contrasts ministerial power with coercive sovereign power: ecclesiastical power is to 'declare' and 'perswade' (proclamation, preaching, teaching) and does not, by Christ's institution, include coercive or sovereign command. This is argued from scriptural metaphors (fishing, leaven, seed), the nature of faith, and Christ's own non-regal example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers lack coercive authority unless endowed with civil sovereign power
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no Coercive Power left them by our Saviour; but onely a Power to proclaim the Kingdom of Christ, and to perswade men... then their Precepts are not Laws; and they have no right of Commanding (unless they also have Soveraign Civill Power by politick institution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments given: (1) Christ's kingdom 'is not of this world' so his ministers cannot require obedience in his name; (2) comparisons to fishing/leaven/seed exclude compulsion; (3) faith cannot depend on compulsion but on persuasion; (4) Scripture passages commanding obedience to earthly princes (Rom.13, 1 Pet.2) preserve civil authority. Thus ministers may punish only when they also hold civil power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apostolic commission enumerates functions but not civil command
rubrics_metrics.description: The points of the Apostles' Commission are to Preach, to Teach, to Baptize, and to remit and retain sins (the Keys), yet 'the points of their Commission, as they are expressely set down in the Gospel, contain none of them any authority over the Congregation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes treats each function (preaching, teaching, baptizing, loosing/binding) as ministerial acts — proclamation, instruction, sacraments, and ecclesiastical discipline — none of which equate to sovereign commands over temporal affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preaching/teaching is proclamation not command
rubrics_metrics.description: Preaching in the original is that act which a Crier, Herald, or other Officer useth to doe publiquely in Proclaiming of a King. But a Crier hath not right to Command any man. 'Bee not called Masters... for one is your Master, even Christ.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes uses the analogy to a public crier to emphasize that the preacher's role is to make known the claim/right of Christ, not to exercise coercive authority; teaching is opening reasons to induce belief and voluntary submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baptisme is a sacrament of allegiance, not the creation of an earthly authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Baptisme is the Sacrament of Allegeance... He that is Baptized, is Dipped or Washed, as a sign of becomming a new man, and a loyall subject to that God... and to acknowledge the Doctrine of the Apostles... we do not in Baptisme constitute over us another authority, by which our externall actions are to be governed in this life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes treats baptism as a symbolic admission into God's kingdom and a pledge to Christ and apostolic doctrine; it does not alter the political allegiance or create new temporal jurisdiction over subjects in the commonwealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to remit and retain sins (Keys) is conditional, dependent on outward marks of repentance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Power of Remission, And Retention Of Sinnes... is not granted simply and absolutely, as God forgiveth, but conditionally, to the Penitent: the Apostles and their Successors are to follow but the outward marks of Repentance; which appearing, they have no Authority to deny Absolution; and if they appeare not, they have no authority to Absolve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because inward repentance is ultimately known only to God, ministers must rely on external signs (words, actions). Hobbes points to Mat.18 (private correction, witnesses, church judgment) and to John 20:22-23 as the scriptural basis; but he stresses limits and conditionality, and warns that feigned repentance makes sacramental absolution ineffective for salvation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgment about repentance belongs to the Church assembly; sentence is pronounced by apostle/pastor as prolocutor
rubrics_metrics.description: The Judgment concerning the truth of Repentance, belonged not to any one Man, but to the Church, that is, to the Assembly of the Faithfull, or to them that have authority to bee their Representant... the pronouncing of Sentence: And this belonged alwaies to the Apostle, or some Pastor of the Church, as Prolocutor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes distinguishes fact-finding (assembly judgment) from formal sentencing (apostle/pastor pronouncement). He cites 1 Cor.5 as practice: assembly hears and judges; apostle/pastor pronounces sentence (e.g., delivery to Satan/exclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excommunication defined and its limited effect without civil enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: To excommunicate, is in the Originall, Aposunagogon Poiein, To Cast Out Of The Synagogue... The Use and Effect of Excommunication, whilest it was not yet strengthened with the Civill Power, was no more, than that they, who were not Excommunicate, were to avoid the company of them that were.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes explains practical consequences: social avoidance (not eating with excommunicates) and exclusion from assemblies only to the extent owners (who are under civil authority) permitted. Without civil backing, excommunication produced social, not civil, penalties; an apostate might return to worldly favour unaffected legally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Martyr defined narrowly as a witness of Christ's resurrection (primary martyrs) — dying for any lesser tenet is not required
rubrics_metrics.description: A Martyr is, (to give the true definition of the word) a Witnesse of the Resurrection of Jesus the Messiah; which none can be but those that conversed with him on earth, and saw him after he was risen... To die for every tenet that serveth the ambition, or profit of the Clergy, is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes distinguishes primary martyrs (original witnesses who saw Christ) from secondary martyrs (who testify only by tradition). Only one article (that Jesus is the Christ risen) merits the title and obligation of martyrdom; others do not justify private disobedience to civil authority or compulsory suffering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faith cannot be compelled; outward profession under compulsion may not constitute true denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Faith is a gift of God, which Man can neither give, nor take away by promise of rewards, or menaces of torture... Profession with the tongue is but an externall thing... If a man be commanded by his lawfull Prince to say with his tongue, wee beleeve not; must we obey such command? Profession with the tongue is but an externall thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes uses the example of Naaman: internal belief remains despite outward gestures done under compulsion. He argues that compelled outward denials are actions of the sovereign, not the subject's inner assent; thus the moral/legal requirement to resist may be different from the private reality of belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apostolic succession/transmission of ecclesiastical power by imposition of hands
rubrics_metrics.description: After our Saviour had breathed upon them... hee addeth... 'Receive the Holy Ghost;' and after his Ascension... the Apostles afterward, transmitted the same Spirit by Imposition of hands, as Moses did to Joshua. So that it is manifest hereby, in whom the Power Ecclesiasticall continually remained, ... namely, in them that received the same from the Apostles by successive laying on of hands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes treats laying on of hands as the sign/seal of commission and the means by which ministerial authority (teaching office and Holy Spirit) is transmitted; he parallels Moses→Joshua with Christ→Apostles→successors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers' authority is subordinate to, and limited by, civil sovereign power
rubrics_metrics.description: It followeth, that Christ, whose authority, as man, was to bee like that of Moses, was no more but subordinate to the authority of his Father... How then can wee be obliged to doe any thing contrary to the Command of the King, or other Soveraign Representant of the Common-wealth... it is manifest, that Christ hath not left to his Ministers in this world, unlesse they be also endued with Civill Authority, any authority to Command other men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes cites scripture (e.g., 'be subject to the Higher Powers' Rom.13; 'submit... to every Ordinance of Man' 1 Pet.2) to justify obedience to civil rulers, and to limit ecclesiastical claims where they conflict with sovereign law. Only when ministers hold civil office may they exercise coercive power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sacraments (Lord's Supper, Paschal Lamb) function as memorials of deliverance and are analogues, not civil constitutions
rubrics_metrics.description: For the other Sacraments, of eating the Paschall Lambe, it is manifestly imitated in the Sacrament of the Lords Supper; in which the Breaking of the Bread, and the pouring out of the Wine, do keep in memory our deliverance from the Misery of Sin, by Christs Passion, as the eating of the Paschall Lambe, kept in memory the deliverance of the Jewes out of the Bondage of Egypt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes emphasizes sacramental symbolism and continuity with Jewish rites; sacraments are religious memorials and rites of admission/commemoration, not mechanisms by which ecclesiastical authorities acquire temporal jurisdiction.
